What this file holds
customers
1000 records · 6 columns
COLUMNS
first_name
taken for string
because no numbering scheme this build carries
accepted 1000 values of this column, and its
header is one this build reads as naming given
names
last_name
taken for string
because no numbering scheme this build carries
accepted 1000 values of this column, and its
header is one this build reads as naming
surnames
birth_date
taken for string
city
taken for string
zip
taken for string
because no numbering scheme this build carries
accepted 1000 values of this column
card
taken for card
because every one of 1000 values of this column
was accepted by the card validator, and by no
other scheme carrying a check digit
Nothing declared what these columns hold, so it
was worked out by looking at the values.
NOT WORKED OUT
Looking at values cannot establish these. Damage
that needs them is still ordered, and the manifest
carries the reason it could not be applied.
maximum length, because the longest value in a
file is not a declared limit, required columns,
because a column with no blanks in it was not
declared to need one, uniqueness, because
values that happen not to repeat were not
declared unique, the set of allowed values of an
enumerated column, which a file never carries,
the primary key, and with it every defect about
the identity of a record, relations between
columns beyond the date and the gender a
numbering scheme encodes, which are the only
two a value can prove without being told,
relations between tables, because one file is one
table, people's names, except in a column whose
header is a common English or Polish word for a
given name, a surname or a full name, such as
first_name, nazwisko or full_name and numeric,
date and postal column types, because a column
of digits is not a column of numbers
